messages.subject: Re: format to use to save a neurolist of dotprops
messages.subject_clean: format to use to save a neurolist of dotprops
messages.body_plain:
Dear Diego,

On Thursday, December 12, 2019 at 3:23:05 PM UTC, Diego A Pacheco Pinedo wrote:
> I was wondering what is the best format to save a collection of dotprops so it can be read/imported again with natverse tools.
> Shoud it be *.SWC even though it does not have any connectivity information?

I recommend to save the neuronlist in R's rds format. If you have a neuronlist object, nl:

saveRDS(nl, file='nl.rds')
# read in later
nl=readRDS('nl.rds')

If you have a very big neuronlist with many thousands of neurons, then you can also use a specialised neuronlist object (neuronlistfh <https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/nat/versions/1.8.13/topics/neuronlistfh>) that only keeps metadata in memory. This can be useful when the objects are approaching (or exceed available memory) since they are read from disk on demand (and usually cached by the operating system). There is an example in that documentation link, but the gist of it is to do:

nlfh=as.neuronlistfh(nl, dbdir='/path/to/my/nl/data') # by convention, save the neuronlisfh object next to filehash  # backing database write.neuronlistfh(nlfh, file='/path/to/my/nl/nlfh.rds') # in a new session nl=read.neuronlistfh("/path/to/my/nl/nlfh.rds")
# plot first 10 neurons - will be read from disk on demand
plot3d(nl[1:10])

To provide a method for distributing neuron databases to end users, neuronlistfh objects can also be provided for download from a URL. They can then transparently download the actual coordinate data for each neuron from a remote server as and when the user tries to access them.

Best wishes,

Greg.

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Re: flycircuit boundingbox
messages.body_plain:
Dear Wenbin,

If you search virtual fly brain for MBON you will get this page:

http://www.virtualflybrain.org/site/stacks/index.htm?id=FBbt_00047953

If you click on images … List All (35) you will get this page.

http://www.virtualflybrain.org/do/individual_list.html?action=exemplar_neuron&id=FBbt:00047953

These images come from a variety of sources (including flycircuit).

For the flycircuit neurons you can read the skeletons using their identifier.

http://natverse.org/flycircuit/reference/fc_read_neurons.html

If you need to do a lot of work of this sort, there is an R package that can do programmatic queries of the VFB website.

https://github.com/jefferis/vfbr
https://jefferis.github.io/vfbr/reference/index.html

Best,

Greg.
